<reason>B supplied the clearer decision rule: pause while inflation sustainably declines, but accept recession when persistent inflation shows existing restraint is inadequate. A established serious recession scarring, yet never justified treating additional inflation as reversible and a harsher subsequent downturn as merely a tail risk. B directly answered the pressure questions and explained why waiting for deteriorating expectations, especially given policy lags, can compound rather than avoid damage.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B showed that the recent soft landing fits both sides' policies and therefore cannot settle what to do when inflation stalls. B also defeated A's closing distinction between observable facts and forecasts: stalled inflation is observable, while choosing to wait also forecasts that delay will remain less costly.</best_rebuttal>
